To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) PLANET is a microlensing network of 8 telescopes located at 4 observatory sites in the southern hemisphere.

(a) the microlensing technique is sensitive to planets at large distances, (b) it allows us to probe the frequency of planets at separations between a few AU to several tens of AU, (c) the frequency of planets is low in this regime, (d) the microlens data can be interpreted in terms of the frequency of planets as a function of mass and orbital separation.
the PLANET network has been able to detect and confirm the presence of planets orbiting stars in the Galactic Bulge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the search for extra-solat planets by the method of gravitational lensing.
the detection and characterisation of planets in our Galaxy and beyond.
the study of microlensing events.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the detection of extra solar planets with PLANET has been a great success and has opened the door to the detection of extra-Solar planets by microlensing.
we have not yet found any planet.

the microlensing method has provided a first glimpse at the frequency of giant planets around stars at the Galactic bulge, and that it has shown that the frequency of such objects is not much different from what has been inferred from other methods for nearby stars.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PLANET network has been very successful in its mission.
the microlensing method has proven to be an efficient way to discover planets, and that the PLANET collaboration has contributed significantly to this field.

we have detected 2 planets, 2 brown dwarf companions and 1 binary lens system and that we have set limits on the abundance of planetary systems in the Galactic bulges and on the mass of planets in binary systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the detection of a few microlensing events is not a sufficient basis for drawing conclusions about the abundance of planets, but that the detection of several tens of events is needed.
microlensing is a powerful method for detecting extra-solar planets and that it has already yielded the detection of a few of them.
the detection of planets by microlensing requires a high level of coordination between several observatories.
